A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EPO research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and complete enough for reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original EPO evaluations on SOTOPIA, WebShop and ALFWorld, together with ablations, self-play experiments and collaboration analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including the single-model SFT comparison.

M1.justification: The strategic LLM, frozen interacting agent, REINFORCE training, binary process rewards and iterative self-play are retained. v1 already specifies maximum-absolute return normalization; v3's explicit formula and on-policy self-play wording do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use SOTOPIA and SOTOPIA-hard, SOTOPIA-pi training scenarios, WebShop, and ALFWorld seen/unseen tasks. The symmetric and asymmetric dialogue scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Vanilla, ReAct, PPDPP, DAT and the same EPO variants. The single-model SFT comparator in v1 Appendix E, Table 9 is retained in v3 Appendix C, Table 6.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported SOTOPIA training budget from 19k steps to approximately 459, and cross-domain WebShop/ALFWorld training from 20k to approximately 650. These substantially revise the stated settings, although the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun or earlier counts were reporting errors.

E4.justification: Table 3's component and backbone ablations, Figure 3's self-play scaling, Figure 4's collaboration analysis, the single-model SFT comparison and Table 10's negotiation case are retained. The new Pareto discussion adds interpretation, not another analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix D in both versions explicitly reports a single run because of computational costs. Neither adds seeds, repeated runs, confidence intervals or significance tests. The revised variance-reduction discussion concerns training rather than statistical reporting.

E6.justification: The result entries in Tables 1–3, Figures 3–4 and the appendix SFT comparison match across versions. Table 10's dialogue and the reported empirical trends are also retained. The revised training budgets are not accompanied by new performance results.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the trajectory tuple and characterizes normalized returns as an advantage and variance-reduction baseline, whereas v1 discusses adding baselines as future work. This changes the mathematical justification of existing normalization; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The main claims about plug-in strategic reasoning, RL with process rewards and self-play, transferability and leading social/web performance remain. v3 removes repeated no-preliminary-SFT wording but retains the pure-RL claim in Sections 2 and 5, principally changing its emphasis.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds a game-theoretic interpretation suggesting that two RL-guided participants approach Pareto optimality while mixed-strength pairs fail to do so. This extends v1's win-win interpretation of the unchanged Figure 4. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The replacement of 19k/20k training steps with approximately 459/650 materially changes the training instructions a reproducer would follow. Other hyperparameters, hardware, model versions, prompts and the promise of a future code/model release are retained.

R1.justification: v3 removes Ahmadian et al. (2024) and adds Williams (2004) for the normalization/baseline discussion and von Neumann et al. (1944) for game-theoretic interpretation. The main related-work section and positioning against existing strategic-reasoning approaches are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in the abstract, method and collaboration discussion, including explanations of partial observability and on-policy self-play. Additional Results moves from Appendix E to C, and Prompts from C to E; most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: All four figure images are identical. Layout changes include moving Table 3 between columns, reformatting appendix prose into two columns, and relocating and renumbering the SFT and prompt tables. Their substantive displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies normalization and on-policy self-play, but adds advantage/baseline and Pareto-optimality interpretations without supporting derivations or additional analyses. Its large training-budget revision is unexplained while the results remain identical. These clarity gains and unresolved technical issues prevent a reliable judgment of net improvement.
